figures.caption: Figure 1: Architecture Diagram. A) Generative Model. B) Causal GRU encodes observations into context trajectory. C) Context trajectory is fed into the branch of a Deep Operator Network along with substeps to produce basis functions. Trunk network can be queried at any z and outputs log ρθ, the unnormalized log density. IC loss between the learned posterior and an IC prior N (0, I) combined with Fokker Planck Residual Loss between observations and Jump Loss at observations D) Posterior Expectation z̄ = Ep(z|x)[z] computed through MALA based MCMC sampling. E) Dynamics and Observation Parameters fit by regressing against z̄

Figure 2: Latent Inference of Simulated Dynamical Systems. A) Exact filtering distribution for the double well system vs filtering posterior distribution estimated by ZENO. B) Latent Posterior Mean Estimate for the Van Der Pol System. C) Latent Trajectory Inference for the Lorenz Attractor. D) Comparison of ZENO’s normalized root mean squared error with the exact optimal filter for each system.

Figure 3: ZENO Drift Estimation Performance. A) True cubic drift of double well (dashed line) overlayed with model estimate. B) True Van Der Pol Vector field (Left) vs Model’s infered Vector Field. C) Lorenz Attractor Dynamics plotted in the xz plane. D) Model’s NRMSE performance compared to baselines. Dots represent seeds and error bars are 1 SD.

Figure 4: Whole-brain calcium dynamics in C. elegans A) Example ZENO reconstruction of RIML neuron. B-C) ZENO recovers limit cycles. D-E) Inferred latents are consistent with known behavioral labels. Model performance compared to baselines on F) reconstruction R2, G) behavior decoding accuracy, and H) forecasting RMSE. Points represent individual worms, separated into NoStim and Stim conditions. Error bars are 1SD.

Table 1: Simulated datasets. d is the latent dimension and D the number of observed channels. G multiplies dW . The observation noise SD ϵ is in physical units for the double well and Van der Pol and in units of the standardized clean signal for Lorenz. Trajectory counts are train / validation / test.
Table 2: ZENO hyperparameters. Shared values apply to every dataset; the last four rows are the only per-dataset settings.

Table 3: gpSLDS hyperparameters. The upper block is shared; the lower block is per dataset. Kato lists the primary configuration (9 of 12 animals; the alternative used for the other three is given in the text).
Table 4: SDE Matching hyperparameters (identical for all datasets unless noted).
Figure 5: Example results for a NoStim worm from the Kato Dataset. See Fig 4A-E

Table 5: Simulated benchmarks: mean ± SD over 5 seeds. Reconstruction R2 and RMSE are against the noiseless signal in standardized units; latent, dynamics and forecasting errors are normalized as defined in Section D.3 (lower is better for all but R2). ZENO scores are filtering estimates; the baselines are smoothers.

Table 6: Kato et al. (2015) per-worm results. N is the number of recorded neurons and T the recording length in seconds. For each method: reconstruction R2 (↑), behavioral decoding balanced accuracy (↑; chance 1/7 NoStim, 1/4 Stim) and forecast RMSE relative to persistence (↓; below 1 beats persistence). “div.” marks a diverged forecast rollout.
